id_darby_canyon.blurb: Darby Canyon is a compact limestone cliff on the Teton range's western flank, reached from the Driggs and Victor side of the valley at roughly 7,000 feet. Nearly all of the 21 climbs here are bolted sport lines, with a single boulder problem and one top-rope line mixed in. Most are fairly short and technical, favoring slab and balance over power, and the grades run from 5.7 up to 5.13 with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.11. The wall faces south and holds sun deep into the afternoon. Expect a small, quiet outing rather than a destination, with more lightly traveled routes further along the cliff.

id_little_cave_the.blurb: Two neighboring sections of a lava tube have fallen in here, leaving a natural stone arch between them, and the bolted lines fill both open pits and the arch itself. It sits on the sagebrush flats north of Shoshone at about 4,570 feet. All 21 routes are sport climbs on basalt, short and bouldery, mostly rated 5.11 and 5.12 with a handful of 5.10s and a few 5.13s at the top end. Routes face northeast, so they see morning sun and fall into shade by late morning. Cold air under the arch makes it a welcome place to cool down between tries. Closed-toe shoes are wise because snakes live in the surrounding lava rock.

id_spice_girls_area.blurb: A boulder sector in the Snake River canyon at Swan Falls in southwest Idaho, wedged between two better-known sectors. It holds 21 problems on the basalt that makes this whole canyon popular. Difficulty is spread widely: about a third are very easy, a good number sit in the V1 to V3 range, and the rest climb through V5 and V6 to a single V7 at the top. The area is quiet and has no tree cover, and the wider canyon is best in spring, fall, winter, or early on summer mornings, since afternoons get hot. Bring pads and expect a short walk in from the dirt parking lot.

id_prow_the.blurb: The Prow is a tall west-facing sport wall on the cliff band overlooking Shoshone Falls, in the Dierkes Lake climbing zone near Twin Falls. Its 21 bolted routes are among the longest in the zone, and a 60 m rope reaches the ground from every one. Grades stretch from 5.8 into the low 5.12s, but the heart of the wall is 5.9 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common. The face stays in shade until about one in the afternoon, which suits warm days. A helmet is a good idea, since the cliff is tall and some rock off the main lines is loose. A cairned path climbs a talus slope to the base, roughly fifteen minutes from the parking area.

id_05_psychedelic_rock.blurb: Psychedelic Rock is a roughly 200-foot limestone cliff in the Mortal Earth section of the Fins, in central Idaho at around 6,500 to 6,800 feet. All 21 climbs are bolted sport routes, mostly 5.10 with a solid group of 5.11s and a few easier lines near 5.8 and 5.9. The rock varies across the face: smooth grey slab on the left, steeper pocketed limestone and chert in the middle, and a dihedral with a roof on the right. Most routes face east and get sun from early morning until roughly one in the afternoon, with a shaded alcove that cools a little sooner. It is the first major cliff reached on the trail, a walk of about fifteen minutes.

id_2_main_section.blurb: The Main Section is the second and largest stretch of the Main Corridor, a basalt cliff band 15 to 25 feet tall on the Tumbleweeds side of the Pocatello bouldering scene, at about 4,800 feet. It holds 21 problems, all bouldering, spanning V0 through V7. The spread leans moderate to hard: a few easy warm-ups, a cluster of V3 and V4 lines, and then V5 to V7 problems for stronger climbers, including two at V7. The cliff runs northwest to southeast and you reach this section by continuing down the band from the start of the corridor, a short walk from the paved path at the trailhead.

id_stairs_right_south.blurb: These are the boulders to the right of the obvious set of steps on the north shore of Dierkes Lake, in the Snake River canyon near Twin Falls. The 21 problems sit on highly featured basalt with pockets, huecos, crimps and slopers, and the trail passes right along them after a short walk of about five minutes. Difficulty covers a wide range: easy problems at V0 and V1, a good number from V2 to V5, and a handful of serious tests up to V10. Dierkes Lake is known as a warm choice for cold months, which makes this a handy winter session close to town.

id_funny_business_wall.blurb: A dark, southeast-leaning wall in the Funny Business Area at Massacre Rocks, a basalt sport-climbing destination on the Snake River Plain in southeast Idaho. It carries 20 bolted routes, nearly all between 5.10 and 5.11 with just one 5.9 and a couple at 5.12 and 5.13, which makes it a standout for climbers working through the moderate grades. Basalt here is steep and featured, with edges, pockets and cracks. In winter the wall soaks up sun until mid-afternoon, so it climbs well on cold days. Summer is usually too hot for comfortable cragging. It is a short walk down from the rim, past two neighboring walls.
